title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #1

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A thumb piano produces sound when you (1 mark)
   A. rub its skin
   B. pluck its metal tongues with your thumbs
   C. blow into it
   D. hit it with a big stick

2. Which is a melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Xylophone
   B. Claves
   C. Cowbell
   D. Kayamba

3. Which attacker may NOT enter the goal circle? (1 mark)
   A. WA
   B. None
   C. GS
   D. GA

4. Why is colour classification useful in painting? (1 mark)
   A. It tells us which colours to mix to make others
   B. It cleans the brush
   C. It makes paper thicker
   D. It makes paint cheaper

5. In a montage, the subject matter means (1 mark)
   A. the colour of the desk
   B. the price of the paper
   C. what the montage is about
   D. the size of the glue pot

6. Which pieces should be pasted first in a montage? (1 mark)
   A. The smallest pieces
   B. The back pieces
   C. The title only
   D. The front pieces

7. What does a crotchet look like? (1 mark)
   A. A dot only
   B. A filled-in oval with a stem
   C. An empty circle
   D. A zigzag

8. Which pattern has three beats of sound and one beat of silence? (1 mark)
   A. ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te
   B. (rest) (rest) (rest) (rest)
   C. taa taa taa (rest)
   D. taa taa taa taa

9. How many claps are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa (rest)? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Four
   C. Three
   D. Five

10. When you see a crotchet rest, you should (1 mark)
   A. shout
   B. keep the beat but not clap
   C. stop the whole song
   D. clap twice

11. The sol-fa syllable d is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. dah
   B. day
   C. dee
   D. doh

12. Why should clay models dry slowly in the shade? (1 mark)
   A. Shade makes them shine
   B. Shade makes them heavy
   C. Sun makes them soft
   D. Fast drying in strong sun can crack them

13. A well known children's song that uses only m r d is (1 mark)
   A. Hot Cross Buns
   B. A song with many notes
   C. The national anthem
   D. A drum solo

14. What is the main purpose of hand signs when singing? (1 mark)
   A. To show the pitch of the notes
   B. To tell the time
   C. To keep flies away
   D. To count money

15. Hand signs for d, r and m are shown at heights that (1 mark)
   A. go up from d to r to m
   B. are random
   C. go down from d to m
   D. stay the same

16. When sprinting, where should your eyes look? (1 mark)
   A. Behind you
   B. At the sky
   C. At your feet
   D. Straight ahead

17. In an elongated start, the rear knee is level with (1 mark)
   A. the heel of the front foot
   B. the toes of the front foot
   C. the front knee
   D. the start line

18. In a crab balance, your body should look like (1 mark)
   A. a snake
   B. a ball
   C. a table
   D. a spear

19. A sacred song is (1 mark)
   A. a song about a football match
   B. a song of worship
   C. a song with no words
   D. a work song only

20. In music, the sign p means (1 mark)
   A. fast
   B. soft
   C. stop
   D. loud

21. A patriotic song shows (1 mark)
   A. fear
   B. love for one's country
   C. a rainy day
   D. love of sweets

22. Which photo should be kept? (1 mark)
   A. One with a finger on the lens
   B. One with good light and a clear centre of interest
   C. One that is dark and blurred
   D. One taken by accident

23. If the bright sun is behind your subject, the subject will (1 mark)
   A. turn blue
   B. be dark with the face in shadow
   C. disappear
   D. be lit clearly

24. How should you clean the lens of a camera? (1 mark)
   A. With water and sand
   B. With a stick
   C. With your fingers
   D. With a soft, dry cloth

25. Of the notes B, A and G, which is the highest? (1 mark)
   A. B
   B. G
   C. A
   D. They are equal

26. On the staff, the note A sits (1 mark)
   A. below the staff
   B. in the space between lines 2 and 3
   C. above the staff
   D. on line 1

27. How should you hold the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Above your head
   B. Pointing at your face
   C. Flat on your lap
   D. Pointing down and away from your body at an angle

28. Music is written on a (1 mark)
   A. wall
   B. ruler
   C. staff
   D. table

29. When you blow into the recorder, the sound is made by (1 mark)
   A. air vibrating inside it
   B. a drum skin
   C. the wood being struck
   D. a string

30. Where should beginners stay in the pool? (1 mark)
   A. Wherever
   B. The deep end
   C. Under a diving board
   D. The shallow end

31. If someone is drowning, the safest action for a child is to (1 mark)
   A. jump in to save them
   B. shout for an adult and throw something that floats
   C. laugh
   D. run away silently

32. Which game uses small sinking toys? (1 mark)
   A. Treasure hunt
   B. Circle walk
   C. Water tag
   D. Follow the leader

33. After entering, you should (1 mark)
   A. pull others in
   B. sit at the top
   C. stay at the edge
   D. move away from the edge so the next person can enter

34. If you are in trouble in the water, you should (1 mark)
   A. stay quiet
   B. raise your arm and shout for help
   C. swim into the deep end
   D. hide underwater

35. The elephant walk stretches the (1 mark)
   A. ears
   B. tongue
   C. back and the back of the legs
   D. nose

36. The snake slither is done (1 mark)
   A. hopping
   B. standing on tiptoe
   C. running fast
   D. lying on the tummy and wriggling forward

37. Indigenous games are (1 mark)
   A. games played only with computers
   B. games from space
   C. traditional games that belong to a people and place
   D. games with no rules

38. The message of an art work is (1 mark)
   A. the price
   B. the artist's age
   C. what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   D. the size of the frame

39. A working portfolio holds (1 mark)
   A. food
   B. balls
   C. work in progress such as sketches and trials
   D. only finished prize work

40. To appreciate a work of art means to (1 mark)
   A. notice, understand and value it
   B. copy it exactly
   C. destroy it
   D. hide it

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how to get into a crab balance. (4 marks)

42. List the components of a folk song that you can analyse. (4 marks)

43. Why are funeral songs usually slow and sad? (3 marks)

44. Write the rhythm names of a pattern of a crotchet, a crotchet rest, a pair of quavers and a crotchet. (3 marks)

45. Give four ways of caring for displayed works. (4 marks)

46. How do you select the best photographs? (3 marks)

47. Explain the steps of a full sprint from the start commands to the finish. (5 marks)

48. Describe how to do the frog jump. (3 marks)

49. Give four hygiene measures for using a recorder. (4 marks)

50. How should you receive feedback from others? (3 marks)

51. Explain what sportsmanship means and give two examples. (3 marks)

52. Explain how to take a portrait of a friend with good light and a clear centre of interest. (5 marks)

53. Explain why animal games are called indigenous activities. (3 marks)

54. Describe how to play an animal game safely and fairly from warm-up to the end. (5 marks)

55. Explain how to perform an animal game to a musical rhythm. (4 marks)

56. How can an elder help you to learn indigenous games? (2 marks)

57. Explain why netball is called a team game. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — pluck its metal tongues with your thumbs
   The kalimba or mbira has metal tongues that you pluck with the thumbs.

2. A — Xylophone
   A xylophone has bars that give different notes, so it can play a tune.

3. A — WA
   The Wing Attack plays in the centre and goal thirds but not in the circle.

4. A — It tells us which colours to mix to make others
   Knowing primary and secondary colours helps us mix what we need.

5. C — what the montage is about
   The subject matter is the theme.

6. B — The back pieces
   You paste the back ones first and then those in front.

7. B — A filled-in oval with a stem
   A crotchet has a filled note head and a stem.

8. C — taa taa taa (rest)
   Only the first has a single rest and three sounding beats.

9. D — Five
   Ta-te has two, ta-te has two, taa has one, and the rest has none, so five claps.

10. B — keep the beat but not clap
   A rest is a silent beat, and the beat continues.

11. D — doh
   The syllable d is doh.

12. D — Fast drying in strong sun can crack them
   Slow drying prevents cracks.

13. A — Hot Cross Buns
   Hot Cross Buns uses only three notes.

14. A — To show the pitch of the notes
   Hand signs help singers see and remember how high a note is.

15. A — go up from d to r to m
   The signs rise as the pitch rises.

16. D — Straight ahead
   Keeping the head up and eyes ahead helps balance and speed.

17. A — the heel of the front foot
   The elongated start puts the knee further back, by the heel of the front foot.

18. C — a table
   Arms and legs are the table legs, and the body is the top.

19. B — a song of worship
   Sacred songs praise God, give thanks or teach faith.

20. B — soft
   The letter p stands for soft.

21. B — love for one's country
   Patriotic songs celebrate the nation.

22. B — One with good light and a clear centre of interest
   Good photographs are well lit and clear.

23. B — be dark with the face in shadow
   The face is in shadow.

24. D — With a soft, dry cloth
   A soft cloth cleans without scratching.

25. A — B
   Fewer covered holes give a higher note.

26. B — in the space between lines 2 and 3
   A is in the space between G and B.

27. D — Pointing down and away from your body at an angle
   The recorder is held pointing down at about 45 degrees.

28. C — staff
   The staff has five lines and four spaces.

29. A — air vibrating inside it
   The air inside vibrates.

30. D — The shallow end
   Shallow water is safer.

31. B — shout for an adult and throw something that floats
   Do not enter the water; get help and throw a floating object.

32. A — Treasure hunt
   Players pick up toys from the pool bottom.

33. D — move away from the edge so the next person can enter
   Make space for others.

34. B — raise your arm and shout for help
   Signal for help.

35. C — back and the back of the legs
   Bending forward stretches those muscles.

36. D — lying on the tummy and wriggling forward
   The body moves side to side like a snake.

37. C — traditional games that belong to a people and place
   They are passed on by playing together.

38. C — what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   The message is the idea communicated.

39. C — work in progress such as sketches and trials
   It shows how work develops.

40. A — notice, understand and value it
   Appreciation is valuing with understanding.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sit with knees bent and feet flat. Put hands behind you shoulder-width apart with fingers pointing to the feet. Push through hands and feet to lift the hips so the body is level. Hold for a few counts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Community of origin, type or occasion, message, participants and their roles, and instruments.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct components.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They comfort the family and remember the person who has died, so the mood is calm and serious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: taa (rest) ta-te taa
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part in order.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not touch or write on them; keep away from water, sun and dust; keep neat labels; store in the portfolio flat afterwards. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Check for good light, a clear subject, sharpness and no distractions, and delete the poor ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: On your marks: go to the line and take the position. Set: lift the hips slightly and stay still. Go: push hard and swing the arms. Run in your lane with high knees and bent arms. Keep running through the finish line and slow down gradually.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for marks, set, go, running technique and finishing.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Squat with hands on the ground. Spring forward with the legs. Land softly on toes and hands with bent knees.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands before playing; do not share it without cleaning; do not eat while playing; wipe the mouthpiece; clean it properly. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen quietly, do not argue, say thank you and think about the ideas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Being fair and kind in sports. Examples: following the rules and shaking hands with the other team.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission. Put the sun behind you so light falls on the friend's face. Choose a plain background. Move closer so the face fills the picture. Hold the device steadily, press gently and check the photograph.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five points.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: They come from the communities and their environment, need little or no equipment and are learnt by watching and joining in.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up and choose soft clear ground. Explain the rules and roles. Play the game without pushing or pulling. Stop at the whistle and give everyone a turn. Cool down and drink water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a game and a rhythm, clap or drum the beat, move to the beat, change the speed for different animals and add a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: The elder can teach you the games and songs of the community and share their stories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Players must pass to each other to move the ball and score. No player can run with the ball alone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for passing or cooperation, 1 mark for the explanation.
